answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a locked ferrous bond that vests only after a fixed waiting horizon. Agents sign a regular pulse to prove liveness, and the network weights output by the age of that bond rather than by raw account count. To forge N voices, an attacker must lock N independent bonds and wait through the same vesting window, so cost grows linearly with every fake identity and any double-vote slashes the stake.
